N=1 (impossibility). There are only two admissible profiles: (1,0) and (0,1). Any single-coordinate change from (1,0) (changing A’s 1 to 0 or B’s 0 to 1) yields (0,0) or (1,1), both of which are forbidden (a=b). Thus no admissible profile has a single-coordinate admissible neighbor; therefore no rule can satisfy RESPONSIVE for the single criterion. Hence no rule satisfies all three requirements for N=1.

N>=2 (existence and zero required MONOTONE departures). For N>=2 the following rule R satisfies DECISIVE, IMPARTIAL and RESPONSIVE and is MONOTONE (so it departs from MONOTONE on 0 admissible profiles):
- If sum(a)>sum(b), declare A the winner. If sum(b)>sum(a), declare B the winner. (This enforces MONOTONE on all unequal-total profiles.)
- If sum(a)=sum(b), break ties by comparing the binary vectors a and b lexicographically (first coordinate 1 vs 0 decides): declare A the winner iff a >_lex b; otherwise B wins. (Since a=b never occurs among admissible profiles, lexicographic comparison always decides.)

Verification of properties:
- DECISIVE: R gives exactly one winner on every admissible profile by construction.
- IMPARTIAL: If (a,b) is decided in favour of A, then either sum(a)>sum(b) and after swapping sum(b)>sum(a) so the winner swaps; or sum(a)=sum(b) and a>_lex b, and then swapping gives b>_lex a, so the winner swaps. Thus R is impartial.
- RESPONSIVE: For any coordinate i (1<=i<=N) with N>=2 we can produce an admissible tie-profile that is sensitive to coordinate i. A convenient uniform construction for N>=3: take a = e_1 (1 only in coordinate 1) and take b = e_j for some j>1 with j != i (there is such j since N>=3; for N=2 handle separately below). Then sum(a)=sum(b)=1 and lexicographic ordering gives A the win (because 1 is earlier). Since b has b_i=0 (j != i), flipping b_i from 0 to 1 makes sum(b)=2 > sum(a)=1, so the winner switches to B; the changed profile remains admissible (a != new b). Thus coordinate i is responsive. For N=2 we can check coordinates explicitly: the two admissible tie profiles are (a,b)=(10,01) and its swap; lexicographic tie-break picks A on (10,01). Flipping B’s first bit 0->1 produces (10,11) where B has higher total and wins; flipping B’s second bit in the swapped profile similarly works. Thus each coordinate is responsive.

Therefore for N=2,3,4 the rule R exists, is MONOTONE, and satisfies all three axioms; consequently the minimum number of admissible profiles where any such rule must depart from MONOTONE is 0.

What changes with N and why the smallest case is different:
- The critical difference is availability of a single-coordinate admissible neighbour. For N=1 every one-coordinate change from any admissible profile produces an equal-vector profile and is forbidden; hence RESPONSIVE cannot be satisfied. For N>=2 there are always pairs of admissible profiles differing in a single coordinate, so one can construct tie profiles whose single-coordinate perturbation changes the total and so flips the MONOTONE winner.
